clue.text: Goes on river feeding scraps

indicators.note: something feeding another is put into its mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: odds and ends are scraps
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A river keeps flowing into some scraps of land or leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The river goes inside, not at the end: it sits just before the final letter of the scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to last or continue, so something that endures goes on.

clue.text: Cut out uniform for one temporarily released

indicators.note: for one means standing in place of the letter that looks like the numeral one

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit is cut, freeing him briefly from service.
explanation.walkthrough: U replaces the I (one) in EXCISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excused from a duty means being let off it for a while.

clue.text: Recklessly strive to finish way out ahead

parts.note: a door is a way out
to die is to finish

explanation.surface: Someone tries desperately to reach the end of a path before others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead' puts the way out before the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Do or die describes an all-out effort where failure is not an option, so a reckless struggle.

clue.text: Poorly trained robbers getting the bird

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters are arranged wrongly

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Clumsy thieves get booed off by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' is slang for being jeered, which hides the literal bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin redbreast is the traditional name for the European robin, a small songbird.

clue.text: Actors in Indian dress caught expressing contempt

indicators.note: in means wrapped inside the garment, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a sari is a draped garment worn in India
the cast are the actors in a play
C is caught in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Performers in saris are spotted sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught is the cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks are mocking ones, used to convey scorn.

clue.text: Coat ordained for use where shooting may occur

parts.note: a film is a thin coat or layer
set in the sense of laid down or decreed

explanation.surface: A garment blessed for wear at a hunt or a firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns, but it is the shooting of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A film set is the place where a movie's scenes are filmed, and filming is called shooting.

clue.text: Spirit apparent at baptism?

parts.note: surface reading: a ghost or holy spirit appearing at a christening
setter's reading: a magical being who is also a sponsor present at a christening

explanation.walkthrough: The first word gives the magical part, and the christening gives the sponsor role of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In fairy tales a magical benefactor attends a baby's christening, combining a sprite with a baptismal sponsor.

clue.text: Exotic title Dave raised on air

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A man named Dave is given an exotic title and lifted up.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise and float in the air without visible support.

clue.text: Jockey puts his foot in it — Queen in ferment

definitions.text: Jockey puts his foot in it

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to stir up is to ferment trouble
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A rider blunders when the Queen is caught up in unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts his foot in it' sounds like a gaffe, but is literal: the rider's foot goes in the stirrup.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop hanging from a saddle that supports a rider's foot.

clue.text: Primary drive, of course, making letters passionate

parts.note: tees are letters T
hot means passionate

explanation.surface: A first drive along the road produces love letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'naturally' but means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the first stroke on each hole is driven from the tee, which is that opening drive.

clue.text: In front of pub press short lever

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a press is a crowd, a throng of people
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Outside a pub, people push forward with a brief heave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of pub' places the shortened word before BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron bar used as a lever for prising things open.

clue.text: Bill's singing well?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a statement of charges for goods supplied
second meaning, read as two words: a singer in good voice

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes Bill a man whose singing is admired; split the answer as IN VOICE for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a document requesting payment, which is what a bill is.

clue.text: Inactive, making little impression during years at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are disordered
during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the letters of years rearranged
a dent is a small impression in a surface

explanation.surface: Years spent idle on a voyage leave hardly any mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like scenery but is the signal to rearrange the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes a life spent sitting down, without much physical activity.

clue.text: Corruption overturned by church firebrand

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, which in a down-reading sense flips the word's order

parts.note: rot means corruption or decay
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A rebellious agitator overturns a corrupt church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firebrand' reads as a radical person, but here it is literal: a burning stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is literally a piece of burning wood carried as a light, which is a torch.

clue.text: Gloomy daughter's back

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A daughter's back is sad and depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning dismal and cheerless.

clue.text: See 3
Hosiery put into pocket in awkward situation

parts.note: tights are a hosiery garment
to pot is to pocket a ball in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: Stockings stuffed into a pocket would leave someone feeling awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put into' suggests one piece goes inside another, but the two simply join; pot means pocket as in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight spot is an idiom for being in a difficult predicament.

clue.text: See 5
Cynical on short trip, took a gamble

indicators.note: short means clipped, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a jaunt is a short pleasure trip
to dice is to gamble with dice

explanation.surface: A jaded traveller bets money on a quick outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaundiced view is bitter and sour, so jaundiced means cynical or resentful.

clue.text: Aussie bird as embraced by sailors

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so this piece goes within the other

parts.note: jacks or jack tars are sailors
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian bird is hugged by a crew of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The laughing jackass is an old name for the kookaburra.
explanation.definitionFit: The laughing jackass is another name for the kookaburra, an Australian kingfisher.

clue.text: Aussie bird pinching clothes up for offence

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards
pinching means grabbing and holding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
garb means clothes

explanation.surface: An Australian bird steals clothes, which counts as a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first, then the whole combination is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so umbrage is a feeling of resentment.

clue.text: Recalled old fiddle in pub game

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is taken in the backward direction

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius, a famous old violin

explanation.surface: Someone remembers an old scam played out during a game at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests a swindle; it is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts, played by throwing at a board on the wall, is a classic game in British pubs.

clue.text: Engineers' undertaking an appeal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a quest is a venture or undertaking

explanation.surface: The engineers' project is appealing for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A request is an act of asking, which is what an appeal is.

clue.text: Editor in pursuit of secret note, oddly fragranced

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so this piece comes after
oddly means take the letters in odd-numbered places

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor chases a secret memo that is strangely perfumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scented means given a pleasant smell, the same as perfumed or fragranced.

clue.text: You could toss this coin and bet every result's heads

indicators.note: heads means the leading letter of each word

parts.note: the leading letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Toss a coin and bet that it lands heads every time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about coin tossing; the definition is the opening four words. Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland Games event in which a tree trunk is thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is a heavy pole thrown end over end in the Highland Games sport called tossing the caber.

clue.text: Queer togs designed for a bizarre person

indicators.note: designed means made to a new pattern, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Odd clothes made for an eccentric character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queer' looks like an anagram signal meaning odd, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a grotesque is a person who is strange, ugly or comically distorted.

clue.text: Look in admiration across lake's shining surface

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so one piece spans round the other

parts.note: to gaze is to look long and admiringly
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone stares in wonder at a lake's glittering surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaze is a glossy coating, such as on pottery, giving a shiny finish.

clue.text: Learning's on the rise, securing new recruit

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means read from bottom to top
securing means holding fast inside, so it wraps round another piece

parts.note: lore is learning or traditional knowledge
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Education is growing, keeping hold of new recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes after the first letter of the upturned word: E-N-ROL.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to sign them up, so to recruit them as a member.

clue.text: A monk embracing bachelor state

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: embracing means holding in its arms, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
BA is Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A monk hugs an unmarried man's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bachelor state' reads as being single; state is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty United States, in the American South.

clue.text: Most troublesome threads unravelled

indicators.note: unravelled means untangled and loose, so the letters come apart and regroup

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Tangled threads come undone and cause the most bother.
explanation.definitionFit: The hardest task is the most difficult one, which is the one giving the most trouble.

clue.text: Senior policeman's sound, but lacking in vision

indicators.note: lacking means without, so those letters are taken away
sound means what is heard when spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: an inspector is a senior police officer; with its first two letters gone, what is left is said like this
the two letters dropped from the front of the officer's rank

explanation.surface: A senior officer seems sound enough but lacks foresight.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking IN from INSPECTOR leaves SPECTOR, which is said like SPECTRE. 'Lacking in vision' looks like one phrase meaning short-sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, and a vision can mean a ghostly apparition.

clue.text: Told within the family

definitions.meaning: first meaning: narrated, as a story is
second meaning: connected by blood or marriage

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a secret shared only among relatives; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of a verb meaning to recount, and also an adjective for kin.
